King.summary: Adopted Dec 2, 2025; in effect Feb 18, 2026 outside shoreline areas. Widths are set by stream type; the County says its fish-bearing widths fall within the average range of site-potential tree height.
King.riparian: Fish-bearing 200 ft in rural areas, 180 ft in urban growth areas; Type N 100 ft; Type O 50 ft (was 115–165 / 65 / 25 ft)

places.name: Seattle
places.summary: Update underway; the city last updated its critical areas code in 2017. No draft yet, and an open house is planned for January 2027 (tentative).
places.riparian: Current: 100 ft on creeks with fish or wildlife habitat (shorelines under separate rules)

places.name: Bellevue
places.summary: Adopted Dec 9, 2025; in effect Jan 1, 2026. Widths are set by stream type, with wider buffers where native plant cover is sparse.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 150 ft, Np 75 ft, Ns 50 ft; 200 / 100 / 67 ft where native cover is sparse and not restored

places.name: Kent
places.summary: Adopted June 16, 2026. Fish-bearing buffers may be reduced by up to 25% with full replanting.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 150 ft, non-fish 100 ft; 50 ft on industrial valley reaches of Mill, Garrison and Springbrook Creeks

places.name: Renton
places.summary: Adopted Dec 8, 2025. Widths are set by stream type, with wider buffers where native plant cover is sparse and not restored.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 115 ft, Np 75 ft, Ns 50 ft; 200 / 100 / 67 ft where native cover is sparse and not restored

places.name: Federal Way
places.summary: We found no critical areas update on official pages; the stream buffer rules date to 2015. The state Commerce Department’s September 2026 status list shows the city’s critical areas update as not yet complete.
places.riparian: Current: fish-bearing 100 ft, Np 50 ft, Ns 35 ft

Kitsap.summary: Adopted Oct 14, 2024; in effect Apr 1, 2025. Wider buffers set by stream type; the state agency’s tree-height method is a voluntary option.
Kitsap.riparian: Adopted ordinance: fish-bearing 200 ft (was 150), non-fish 100 ft (was 50), Type O 50 ft; 150 / 75 ft option for some urban projects

Pierce.summary: Adopted Dec 3, 2024 with the County’s periodic update; in effect Feb 1, 2025. Wider buffers set by stream type.
Pierce.riparian: Fish-bearing 175 ft (was 150), Np 115 ft, Ns 100 ft, Type O 65 ft

places.name: Tacoma
places.summary: Adopted July 14, 2026. Widths assume dense native plant cover; where cover is sparse, a project must enhance the buffer under an approved plan.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 150 ft (was 100–150 ft); non-fish 100 ft (was 25–100 ft); 200 ft on salmon-bearing “streams of local significance” outside shoreline areas (was 150 ft)

Snohomish.summary: Adopted May 14, 2025. In Feb 2026 the state Growth Management Hearings Board sent the stream buffers back for revision by Dec 17, 2026; the County’s draft response widens them. The Planning Commission hearing on it was set for Oct 27, 2026; we found no later hearing date posted.
Snohomish.riparian: Proposed fish-bearing 200 ft (180 ft for some urban projects), non-fish 100 ft (now 150 / 50 ft)

places.name: Everett
places.summary: Adopted Apr 15, 2026; in effect June 1, 2026. One 100-ft standard buffer on fish-bearing and non-fish streams, wider where vegetation is sparse.
places.riparian: 100 ft on fish-bearing and non-fish streams; 150 / 125 ft where vegetation is sparse and not restored (non-fish was 50 ft)

Clallam.summary: Critical areas update underway, separate from the 20-year plan update. The Planning Commission is reviewing a draft section by section; an Oct 7, 2026 staff memo offers wider stream buffers, set by project impact, for discussion.
Clallam.riparian: Staff options for discussion (Oct 7, 2026): fish-bearing 100–200 ft and non-fish 80–150 ft by project impact; now 60–150 ft on fish-bearing streams (by stream type and project size) and 50 ft on non-fish streams (shorelines under separate rules)
Clallam.next: Planning Commission critical areas review Nov 18, 2026, 6 pm

Clark.summary: Critical areas rules were updated in March 2023, using the state agency’s tree-height method for fish-bearing streams. The 20-year plan adopted Oct 13, 2026 leaves them unchanged. The state Commerce Department’s status list, marked “Last Updated: September 2026,” shows the critical areas update as not yet complete.
Clark.riparian: Fish-bearing 150–235 ft and Np 100–155 ft by site class (soil productivity); Ns 100 ft (was 200 / 100 / 75 ft)

places.name: Vancouver
places.summary: Adopted Dec 9, 2024. One width for all stream types, based on tree-height averages.
places.riparian: Adopted 2024: 185 ft on fish-bearing and non-fish streams alike, a 100-ft management area plus an 85-ft outer buffer where development is allowed if it meets performance standards; the state tree-height tool may justify less on constrained sites (was 125–175 ft)

Island.summary: Critical areas update started after the 20-year plan was adopted June 23, 2026; the County last updated these rules in 2019. Staff told commissioners on Oct 14, 2026 that stream buffers should be updated for the state fish and wildlife agency’s tree-height method; no draft yet.
Island.riparian: Current: fish-bearing 100 ft, other streams 75 ft

Jefferson.summary: Adopted Mar 9, 2026, separate from the 20-year plan, and in effect the same day. Non-fish stream buffers widened to 100 ft, and rural fish-bearing buffers to 200 ft.
Jefferson.riparian: Fish-bearing 200 ft in rural areas, 150 ft in urban growth areas and LAMIRDs, the more developed rural areas (was 150 ft); Np 100 ft (was 75); Ns 100 ft (was 50–75 ft by slope)

Lewis.summary: Adopted Dec 9, 2025 as the last step of the periodic update, after the 20-year plan (Sept 23, 2025). Commissioners kept 75-ft buffers on non-fish streams instead of the proposed 100 ft.
Lewis.riparian: Fish-bearing 150 ft (100 ft on streams under 10 ft wide, with a qualified professional’s report); Np and Ns 75 ft (shorelines under separate rules)

Mason.summary: Critical areas update (the County’s Resource Ordinance) follows the 20-year plan adopted in December 2025. The draft widens fish-bearing and seasonal-stream buffers; the Planning Advisory Commission recommended approval after its Aug 31, 2026 hearing.
Mason.riparian: Proposed: fish-bearing 185 ft (now 150), Np 100 ft, Ns 100 ft (now 75), plus a 15-ft building setback; a site tree-height study may set the fish-bearing width, never under 100 ft (shorelines under separate rules)
Mason.next: County commissioners public hearing Nov 10, 2026, 9:15 am

San Juan.summary: Critical areas update underway, separate from the 20-year plan adopted Dec 9, 2025; the current rules date to 2013. The final draft replaces slope-based water quality buffers with fixed stream buffers. The Planning Commission and the state Department of Ecology held a joint public hearing Oct 16, 2026; no Council date is posted yet.
San Juan.riparian: Proposed: fish-bearing 180 ft, Np 100 ft, Ns 100 ft (now: fish-bearing 50–150 ft water quality buffer by slope and land use, plus a 110-ft tree protection zone; Np 50 ft and Ns 30 ft tree protection zones)

Skagit.summary: Adopted Nov 25, 2025, separate from the 20-year plan. In July 2026 the state Growth Management Hearings Board sent the stream buffers back for revision by Jan 19, 2027; the County’s draft response adds tree-height riparian zones.
Skagit.riparian: Adopted 2025: fish-bearing 150 ft (was 100–150 ft by stream width), Np and Ns 100 ft (was 50). Proposed: these become baseline widths, and the protected buffer extends up to one tree height where that zone is densely vegetated
Skagit.next: Planning Commission public hearing Nov 17, 2026, 6 pm (written comments to Nov 19)

Thurston.summary: Critical areas update underway, separate from the 2045 plan adopted Dec 16, 2025. The Oct 7, 2026 draft replaces stream-type widths with the state agency’s tree-height method.
Thurston.riparian: Proposed: one 200-year site-potential tree height, at least 100 ft (now 100–250 ft by stream type)
Thurston.next: Hearing draft overview and open house Nov 18, 2026; Planning Commission public hearing anticipated Dec 2, 2026

Whatcom.summary: Critical areas update started, separate from the 20-year plan adopted July 28, 2026; the County last updated these rules in 2017. No draft yet: Planning Commission workshops on riparian zones are under way, with adoption planned before March 2, 2027.
Whatcom.riparian: Current: fish-bearing 150 ft, Np and Ns 50 ft; Type S streams 200 ft
Whatcom.next: Planning Commission workshop Nov 19; public hearing Dec 10, 2026

Benton.summary: Planning Commission hearing held Oct 6, 2026. The final draft for the commissioners, posted Oct 22, 2026, keeps the proposed 100-ft stream buffers; the County cited the state fish and wildlife agency’s guidance.
Benton.riparian: Proposed 100 ft minimum on fish-bearing and non-fish streams (now 75 ft fish-bearing, 50 ft non-fish, or 100 ft where the stream has adjacent slopes of 10% or more; shorelines under separate rules)
Benton.next: Commissioners’ hearing Nov 3, 2026, 9 am, Courthouse, Prosser

places.name: Kennewick
places.summary: Adopted Sept 15, 2026. The state fish and wildlife agency had recommended at least 100 ft.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 75 ft, non-fish 50 ft (unchanged)

places.name: West Richland
places.summary: Draft critical areas code sets buffers by stream type, with a 15-ft building setback. It went to the council for acceptance on Oct 20, 2026.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 100 ft, Np 50 ft, Ns 25 ft
places.next: Planning Commission hearing Jan 6, 2027; council hearing and adoption Jan 26, 2027 (tentative)

places.name: Richland
places.summary: A city flyer in the Planning Commission’s Oct 28, 2026 packet says the critical areas update “will occur in early Spring” 2027, after the plan update.
places.next: City expects plan adoption in December 2026; Planning Commission hearing on the plan was set for Oct 28, 2026 (outcome not yet posted)

Chelan.summary: No critical areas amendments found in the County’s 2026 update; its current rules date to 2021.
Chelan.next: Planning Commission Oct 28; written comments due Nov 3; commissioners’ hearings Nov 10, 2026

places.name: Wenatchee
places.summary: The city’s 2026 package does not include its critical areas title.

Cowlitz.summary: The County’s posted code is stamped adopted Sept 1, 2026, effective Dec 1, 2026. Wider stream buffers by stream type.
Cowlitz.riparian: Fish-bearing 180 ft; non-fish 100 ft (25 ft for tiny seasonal channels); was 100 / 50 ft

places.name: Kelso
places.summary: Draft uses the state fish and wildlife agency’s tree-height zones. Planning Commission hearing held Oct 13, 2026.
places.riparian: 25 to 235 ft by stream type and site class (25 ft only on ephemeral non-fish channels)

places.name: Longview
places.summary: Update underway; fish and wildlife buffers flagged for change; no draft posted.
places.riparian: Current: 50 to 200 ft by stream type

Douglas.summary: Draft critical areas code published July 16, 2026; comments closed Sept 25. The draft sets no stream buffer widths of its own. An Oct 16, 2026 staff report says the County intends to update its critical areas rules after the plan update.
Douglas.riparian: No stream widths in the draft; it sends streams to its wetland chapter, which sets widths only for wetlands
Douglas.next: Planning Commission hearing on the County plan Nov 4; commissioners Dec 8 and 15, 2026 (tentative)

places.name: East Wenatchee
places.summary: Draft critical area code amendments published July 11, 2026. Staff say they will be finished in this update; they are not part of the Oct 28 joint hearing.
places.riparian: Sand Canyon 75 ft plus a 15-ft setback (unchanged in the draft)
places.next: No hearing date posted for the critical areas amendments

Franklin.summary: Plan chapters are in Planning Commission review; no critical areas draft found. County slides from Sept 30, 2026 say the critical areas update, mainly for shrub-steppe, will come in 2027.

places.name: Pasco
places.summary: Critical areas update (file CA2025-005). The draft sets no stream buffers of its own: the city says all its riparian areas are shorelines under separate rules. The state fish and wildlife agency recommended at least 100 ft and, in an Oct 23 email, said it and the city would review two possible streams outside shoreline areas.
places.riparian: None in the critical areas code; the city says all its riparian areas are shorelines under separate rules
places.next: Planning Commission hearing Oct 29, 2026, 6:30 pm; council action planned November 2026 (tentative)

Kittitas.summary: Adopted June 16, 2026. Stream buffers follow the state agency’s tree-height method, set in a 2025 amendment.
Kittitas.riparian: Fish-bearing and Np: one site-potential tree height, at least 100 ft; Ns 100 ft

places.name: Ellensburg
places.summary: The city’s 2026 code package does not amend its critical areas rules.
places.next: Council hearing Nov 2, 2026; final adoption Nov 16 (tentative)

Skamania.summary: Joint County and Stevenson draft keeps today’s buffers, with a formal explanation of why it departs from the state agency’s wider guidance. Hearing held Oct 12, 2026.
Skamania.riparian: Fish-bearing 100 ft, Np 50 ft, Ns 25 ft (unchanged)

places.name: Stevenson
places.summary: Plans to adopt the County’s critical areas rules by reference.
places.riparian: Same as the County draft
places.next: Planning Commission hearing Nov 9, 2026, 6 pm, City Hall

Spokane.summary: Draft critical areas code published; the Planning Commission hearing opened July 16, 2026. The Commission’s Nov 12 agenda, posted Oct 28, has no critical areas item. Wider flat buffers by stream type.
Spokane.riparian: Proposed fish-bearing 150 ft, non-fish 100 ft (now 100 / 75 / 25 ft)
Spokane.next: No critical areas hearing date posted; after Nov 12, the Planning Commission next meets Dec 3, 2026

places.name: Spokane
places.summary: The city plans to update its critical areas rules after its 2026 plan update; no draft yet.
places.riparian: Current: fish-bearing 150–250 ft, non-fish 150 ft (shorelines under separate rules)
places.next: Plan Commission hearing on the plan Nov 9, 2026 (tentative)

places.name: Spokane Valley
places.summary: Draft code (Sept 18, 2026) sets creek-by-creek widths, with an option to use the state tree-height tool where it gives a smaller width. Planning Commission hearing held Oct 22, 2026; its recommendation is not yet posted.
places.riparian: Chester Creek 115 ft, Saltese Creek 125 ft, 100 ft default (now 150 / 50 / 30 ft)
places.next: Council hearing Dec 1; adoption vote Dec 15, 2026 (tentative)

Walla Walla.summary: The County’s periodic update is underway; no critical areas draft is posted yet. Its current code already sets creek buffers by named reach, from 35 ft to 100 ft. The County says the update will include “updated maps, buffers, and mitigation standards.”
Walla Walla.riparian: Current: tiered by reach, 35 / 50 / 75 / 100 ft (County code 18.08.650)
Walla Walla.next: County says its draft critical areas code comes after a draft environmental review due in early 2027; hearings continue through spring 2027

places.name: City of Walla Walla
places.summary: Draft raises most creek buffers from 35 ft (50 on Yellowhawk) to 100 ft plus a 15-ft setback. After an Oct 14 hearing, Council asked staff for options no earlier than Nov 4 and by the end of November.
places.riparian: Flat 100 ft on every creek it covers (Mill Creek under shoreline rules)

places.name: College Place
places.summary: The city’s Oct 20, 2026 code draft would adopt the County’s critical areas code by reference. A full critical areas review, including stream buffer options, is expected by Dec 31, 2027.
places.riparian: Would use the County’s creek buffers (now 35–100 ft by named reach)
places.next: Council workshop Oct 27; Planning Commission hearing Nov 17, 2026, 6 pm; Council hearing date not set

places.name: Waitsburg
places.summary: Draft plan and code went to the state in May 2026. The draft code keeps the existing creek buffers.
places.riparian: Touchet River 25 ft, Coppei Creek 15 ft (draft keeps current)

Yakima.summary: Draft critical areas title (Aug 17, 2026) with wider, tiered buffers; Planning Commission hearings held Aug 26 and Sept 23. Next date not set.
Yakima.riparian: Proposed 150 ft on Type 1–2 streams (200 ft or tree height on salmon, steelhead and cold-water reaches), 100 ft on Type 3, 50 ft on Type 4 (now 100 / 100 / 50 / 25 ft)

places.name: City of Yakima
places.summary: The city’s 2026 package does not include a critical areas update.

Adams.summary: 2027–2047 update underway; no critical areas draft found.

Asotin.summary: No public critical areas update materials found.

Columbia.summary: County draft (part of a joint update with Dayton and Starbuck) reviewed by the Planning Commission Oct 12, 2026. It sets one 100-ft width for streams outside shoreline areas; the Commission will compare it with the tree-height method before choosing. Starbuck’s draft code adopts the County’s rules; whether they will apply inside Dayton is not yet clear.
Columbia.riparian: Proposed flat 100 ft (now 75–150 ft; 50 ft on small and non-fish streams)
Columbia.next: Planning Commission Nov 9, 2026, 5:30 pm; revised draft back to the Commission January 2027; adoption planned March–June 2027

Ferry.summary: Draft plan and development code posted July 2026.
Ferry.riparian: Draft table: shoreline 150 ft, fish-bearing 100 ft, non-fish 50 ft

Garfield.summary: Joint County and Pomeroy update; no critical areas draft is public yet.

Grant.summary: Update underway with Planning Commission workshops; no critical areas draft found.

Grays Harbor.summary: The Planning Commission recommended the new land use plan in October 2026 after hearings in August and September; no critical areas draft found.

Klickitat.summary: Critical areas update began in 2022; in Nov 2024 the County withdrew its 2022 environmental determination and issued a new one on an updated draft. No adoption found; the County still posts its 2013 critical areas ordinance.

Lincoln.summary: Science review dated Aug 2026; a public draft was expected in October (tentative).

Okanogan.summary: Critical areas update under contract through June 2027; no draft found.

Pacific.summary: Draft critical areas amendments (June and Aug 2026) widen stream buffers; comment period ended.
Pacific.riparian: Proposed fish-bearing 150 ft (from 130), non-fish 100 ft (from 50–65), tree-height option with a 100-ft floor
Pacific.next: Planning Commission workshop on the plan’s critical areas chapter Nov 5, 2026, 6 pm, Long Beach (no code hearing set)

Stevens.summary: A working draft critical areas code was posted for the Planning Commission’s Oct 22, 2026 meeting. It replaces stream-type widths with one 100-ft streamside zone outside shoreline areas; no hearing date is set.
Stevens.riparian: Proposed flat 100 ft on every stream outside shoreline areas (now 65–100 ft by stream type, slope and zoning)

Wahkiakum.summary: Draft plan review finished July 2026; no critical areas draft found.

Whitman.summary: Commissioners approved critical areas amendments June 29, 2026. Follow-up work is underway: floodplain changes the Planning Commission recommended Oct 7, 2026, and minor revisions to the critical areas code.
Whitman.riparian: Drafts: fish-bearing 180 ft, non-fish 100 ft (up to 180 ft on unstable slopes), tree-height option never below 100 ft; the drafts replace 150–225 ft defaults
Whitman.next: Planning Commission workshop Jan 20, 2027; hearing Mar 17, 2027 (draft schedule)
